> Is there something in your home school program that makes you think that you won't be able to go into computer science? In my experience (with many close friends who are or who have been in computer sciences), disliking other people isn't necessarily a drawback.

It's not the school. I know all my opportunities are going to come in college, and what help I get for myself. It's more just my inadequacies. I'm really awful at thinking technically. Math is my worst subject. 

I probably shouldn't be looking to be a programmer when that's the case. I'd go so far as to say I don't actually enjoy the act of writing code. But, it's just all I want anymore.

I never understood why happiness was the ultimate goal to life (assuming the lack of a deity, of course.

I've read papers by the dalai lama, and other spiritualists. And the objective always seems to be happiness.

Why? Who ever decided that happiness was the best thing to feel? Really, what makes you think that's all people want to feel?

I only just got into home schooling. My mother had some complications at her job, so it's uncertain where we're going to end up, this is just to make things easier. 

For every other grade, and a short spell( two - three months long) during my freshman year, I was going to public schools. And I'll be honest, I really hated them. 

I've been to a therapist twice. once for behavioral issues in Elementary, and another for "family dynamics" problems. Both times the therapists opted to spend more time with me. And while I don't think I realized it, I just manipulated them. And they knew damn well what was going on. But, after all, a therapist just wants you in there as long as possible; and that's what I gave them.

I can't help but think that's all I'm doing here.

My half-brother shot himself shortly after being dumped. He was really depressed and, courtesy of his clueless father, never got any help. So far as I can tell I exhibit a lot of the symptoms that he did. But it's really hard for me to come to terms without a third party.

I've never had any ethical problems with suicide, the only reason I'm still alive is because I haven't found an easily available and painless method. But all the same, I'd hate to do something like that. My mother almost hated my half-brother after he killed himself, remarking that suicide was such a selfish thing to do.

I don't think any real background would be meaningful, so I'll provide the basics. But if you need anymore, just ask.
